items.author: TOI WORLD DESK

items.title: Dollar jumps after strong US payrolls report
items.description: The US dollar index jumped significantly following the Labor Department's report indicating an increase of 165,000 jobs last month, which far exceeded economists' forecasts. As a result, the probability of a rate hike from the Federal Reserve climbed to nearly 80% for next month. Moreover, Federal Reserve officials voiced concerns about ongoing inflation, leading to declines for other currencies such as the euro and sterling against the dollar.

items.title: Gold drops as strong US payrolls boost dollar, yields
items.description: In light of stronger-than-anticipated US payroll figures, gold prices dipped significantly as the data suggested a robust labor market. This development heightened expectations for sustained high-interest rates from the Federal Reserve, bolstering the dollar's strength. Spot gold saw a decline of 0.3% to reach $4,074.36 per ounce, while US gold futures fell by 0.9%. However, Indian retail demand picked up ahead of Diwali festivities, taking advantage of the lower prices.

items.title: California neighbours fight over garage space; $292,544 legal fee claim denied
items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: In a contentious parking dispute in Orange County, condominium owners WCST Enterprises and Berit Ling faced off in court. Ultimately, the court ruled in favor of WCST, affirming its claim to garage space 38G-a. However, despite the legal victory, WCST could not reclaim its substantial legal fees of $292,544, as these claims did not meet California statutes for fee recovery.

items.title: Idaho family's 125-year-old ranch protects 1,686 acres for migrating deer
items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: A conservation easement has been established on the Flying A Ranch in Idaho to protect the land. This easement allows the Atchley family to continue their farming operations while preventing future development. The agreement also supports a crucial wildlife migration corridor for mule deer and various other species. Previous efforts to protect the ranch were led by Clen Atchley, who passed away in 2024.
